note: RFC4271 Section 5 requires a previous AS's Partial bit to survive on a recognized optional-transitive attribute that is accepted and passed along. The two tagged storage tests exercise only unrecognized attributes 250/251 through OtherAttrs, including length reframing; they preserve useful proof but do not demonstrate this recognized-attribute requirement. The reactor test demonstrates recognized COMMUNITY preservation at enforceRFC7606, and the core walk test demonstrates an already-E0 recognized COMMUNITY remaining unchanged with zero new stamps. The core negative tag is another conforming preservation case, not a violating input or a distinct normative negative. These scopes do not justify the legacy assurance of recognized storage and whole forwarding. The new untagged storage, selected-capture, AS4 and automatic-rewrite regressions and reviewed repairs supply additional bounded component evidence, but they do not expand the current tagged claim or establish recipient-visible preservation through real Session admission, authorized selected/recovery delivery and the final writer. C0 twins, ignored-companion cases, legal suppression and well-known/non-transitive Partial clearing remain useful controls; they are not normative negatives for this sentence. Whole-row assurance is therefore weak. The requirement remains applicable with its full ID, level and quote; no existing input, assertion, tag or recorded proof is removed by this audit correction. Tag/polarity correction and matching native proof integration remain separate, unapplied work.
